content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 Pager — SRV lookup error spike detected in eu-central-1a (service-discovery). Error rate > 40% for SRV queries to model-router.cluster.local, started ~15m ago. @maya (oncall) paged.

maya (oncall): Ack. Jumping in. Any frontend/ingress alerts?

jae (sre): We're seeing elevated 5xx from control-plane components that depend on SRV lookups. TTLs look fine but many SRV queries return SERVFAIL or timeouts to CoreDNS pods in eu-central-1a.

priya (eng-runtime): Confirmed from app-side: fallback to static route sometimes succeeds but adds ~600ms. Impact: model inference latencies and occasional 502s. Putting initial customer-impact note in support thread.

carmen (support): Notified a couple enterprise customers via DM that we’re investigating higher latencies and sporadic errors. No broad support tickets yet.

maya (oncall): Good. jae/priya take lead on infra triage. I'll open a bridge and update customers.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://zoom.redwood/incident/3159991111 — incident-commander: maya. Severity: P1. Runbook template attached.

jae (sre): Quick triage outputs:
```
# from kube exec into coredns pod eu-central-1a
$ kubectl -n infra logs coredns-5d6f7bb9
[..]
E[SRV] lookup model-router.cluster.local: lookup error: i/o timeout
E[GRPC] downstream: failed to resolve SRV: SERVFAIL
```
We have 3 CoreDNS pods in eu-central-1a; CPU and mem are fine. Network egress to consul endpoints shows increased RTT and occasional packet loss.

priya (eng-runtime): Consul agent logs on a couple nodes show intermittent connect failures to local consul server: `error: consul rpc dial timeout` — could be AZ fabric issue. Cross-checking cloud provider's maintenance events...

alex (platform): I'm seeing a networking flap reported on the fabric for eu-central-1a — several spine switches had transient neighbor resets around the same time. Provider status page shows partial degraded peering for that AZ (not full outage).

maya (oncall): Hypothesis: partial network partition between app nodes + service discovery mesh causing SRV queries to fail intermittently. Plan: 1) Fail traffic from eu-central-1a to eu-central-1b (safe AZ failover) for control-plane SRV queries. 2) Scale coredns replicas in other AZs, 3) Temporarily pin model-router to healthy zone via routing policy. Any objections?

jae (sre): +1. Also recommend clearing CoreDNS cache to avoid stale negative entries after flaps: `kubectl exec -n infra coredns-5d6f7bb9 -- coredns-ctl cache flush` (batch across pods).

priya (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a small routing policy change in the service mesh to prefer eu-central-1b/c for service-discovery control traffic. Will stage a canary first.

alex (platform): I'll open a cloud-network ticket and request expedited peering checks. Also will add a temporary route reweight for SRV queries at the LB layer (5m window with rollback).

maya (oncall): Doing the roll now:
- execute traffic reweight to prefer eu-central-1b (control-plane SRV)
- scale coredns in eu-central-1b from 2 -> 5
- flush coredns caches in eu-central-1a and b

deploy-bot: Traffic policy update deployed by maya@ops at commit a12f9e3 — rollout started.

priya (eng-runtime): Canary is green on 10% of control queries. Latency down from 600ms to ~120ms for canary hosts.

jae (sre): After cache flush and reweight, SRV error rate reduced from 42% -> 6% in the next 6m. Noted a few residual back-pressure events but mostly stable.

carmen (support): Messaging update: sent out status to impacted customers: short maintenance window, partial AZ networking degradation, using routing policies to mitigate. No action required by customers.

maya (oncall): Moving to mitigation phase. Assigning follow-ups:
- jae: continue monitoring SRV error rate and rollout automated failover if >10% in next 30m
- priya: collect eval prompts to detect any quality regressions due to route change
- alex: continue cloud network escalation; request root cause timeline from provider
- carmen: track any incoming support tickets and escalate urgent ones to bridge

jae (sre): Setting alert: if SRV error rate > 10% for 5m then auto-trigger full zone failover and notify oncall.

priya (eng-runtime): Adding a short-term mitigation in runtime: enable SRV aggressive retry + jitter to smooth client behavior (config toggle rolled to 50% then 100%).

incident-bot: Pager duty: handoff scheduled at 2026-03-15T02:00Z to night-oncall (sam). Current commander: maya.

maya (oncall): we’ll keep bridge open for 60m monitoring, then step down to watch mode if stable. Next update in 20m or on any regression.

alex (platform): Provider confirmed packet loss on fabric for 12m window; they're running hardware swap. ETA for full clear: ~2h. We'll keep routing policy in place until clear.

jae (sre): Post-mitigation tasks: collect coredns metrics, consul rpc metrics, and produce a short RCA doc outlining why negative caches propagated and why our SRV fallback wasn't faster. Planning to stub RCA in /incident-postmortems/3159991111.json

maya (oncall): Thanks team. Great response. :thumbsup: Closing this thread on Slack — moving notes to incident bridge and RCA channel.

deploy-bot: Audit: scaled coredns eu-central-1b to 5 replicas, cache flush executed across 6 pods, traffic reweight rollback set to auto after 2h.

carmen (support): Placed follow-up email to customers summarizing mitigation and expected update after provider repair.

sam (night-oncall): Acked handoff. Will watch alerts and escalate if error > threshold.
